Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 2) demonstrates bilateral pulmonary nodules and prominent hilar regions, which, when correlated with the CT finding of conglomerate lymphadenopathy (Figure 1a), is characteristic of sarcoidosis. This pattern of bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy combined with parenchymal nodules corresponds to the "sarcoid galaxy sign" described in option B, distinguishing it from unilateral processes like TB or lymphoma, or non-nodular patterns like heart failure.
